notes: Dev ABox revision on aria_in (staging/literature_arts.RELATIONS.md): an aria belongs to one opera (functional), is part of it (aria_in ⊑ part_of) and of every work the opera is part of (aria_in ∘ part_of ⊑ part_of), and is by the opera's composer (aria_in ∘ composed_by ⊑ composed_by). The record used part_of before, which is not functional, so nothing licensed the related-near 'no' (review 2026-11-11, must fix). 'Nessun dorma' moves from Turandot into Die Walküre. Related near asks whether Turandot still includes it: no, because aria_in is functional (the prompt no longer names Puccini). Related far asks its composer, a stored answer (Puccini): the role chain through Die Walküre gives Wagner, and composed_by being functional drops Puccini; it is labelled chain, since a relation property carries it, not composition. Derived: the Ring cycle by transitivity of part_of once the subproperty gives part_of (alt_derivations: chain, aria_in ∘ part_of ⊑ part_of), the same opera as the 'Ride of the Valkyries' (composition), and the language of the libretto of the opera that contains it (composition: a stored fact about Die Walküre, Italian to German). The century question was dropped: it needed an unlisted premise (a part of an opera was written when the opera was) that is not firm, since arias can be written apart from their opera. The edit statement names no composer, so the composer question needs the bridge. Related near uses functional, not inverse: has_part is many-valued, so no 1-hop inverse question has one stored answer that the edit changes. Unrelated near asks another famous aria's opera (Carmen), which differs from the new answer.
